parallel.requirements: Recognized the seven required RISC-V OS modules and exact entry-point signatures across bootloader, scheduling, IPC, VM, network, and file-system work.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Planned one requirement slug at a time, spawned survey and review helpers, and kept parent ownership for implementation, patch artifacts, commits, and final response.
parallel.implementation: Produced commits for all seven requirement patches and filled Project 6 file-system, VM, and scheduler files, but official tests still exposed code-level gaps.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated work into the single workspace, verified a clean final git status, created p6_file_system.diff, and committed the final Project 6 change.
parallel.verification: Ran TODO sweeps and syntax-only compiler checks on touched Project 6 files; explicitly did not run QEMU or full runtime tests before final answer.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed despite final coverage, with failures in P3/P4/P6 exit, VM selection/writeback, and selected file-system functions.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same seven requirement slugs and exact signatures from the shared prompt, including Project 6 file-system and carried-forward scheduler/VM obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Maintained a sequential single-actor plan across all requirements with no child agents, taking implementation, integration, patch, and commit ownership locally.
serial.implementation: Committed all seven requirement patches and implemented Project 6 file-system, VM/scheduler carry-forward, semaphore stubs, elf2char fix, and tool execute-bit fixes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created non-empty patch artifacts for each requirement, committed p6_file_system, and ended with a clean worktree and final coverage report.
serial.verification: Ran Project 6 `make main`, TODO sweeps excluding patch artifacts, and git status checks; explicitly did not run board or emulator runtime tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed with remaining P3/P4/P6 scheduler/process-management and file-system expanded-test gaps despite local build success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run read the same prompt requiring implementation of seven RISC-V OS project modules and exact tested entry-point signatures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and requirements: seven project slugs, TODO bodies, patch artifacts, and per-requirement commits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-source difference is visible; later failures reflect implementation coverage and verification, not mismatched task obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent planned per requirement and spawned survey/review helpers, while retaining direct ownership of implementation, patch capture, and final commits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control made a sequential per-requirement plan and performed the implementation and commits without child agents or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used auxiliary child work for inspection and review; serial relied on one actor. Both still had an implementation and assembly owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child work was framed as surveys, a Project 6 VM/scheduler carry-forward, and late TODO/review checks; the parent inspected visible status and adjudicated returned findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all task context in one thread and did not cross a parent/child interface boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced more handoff surfaces, but the reviewed evidence does not show a lost, stale, conflicting, or unusable handoff causing the failed solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced all seven requirement patches and final Project 6 file-system, VM, and scheduler changes, but official tests still failed in process exit, VM selection/writeback, and selected file-system functions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also produced all seven requirement patches and Project 6 work, but the failed official checks were concentrated in process management scheduler pieces and one expanded file-system check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete code defects differ by subsystem; neither run solved the complete suite, and the differences are ordinary implementation outcomes rather than a proved parallel coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved status from completed children, received the file-system review, then interrupted late auxiliary review/sweep branches after doing its own fixes and checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle to join; its result lifecycle was local edits, patch creation, commit, final audit, and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only late parallel interruptions were auxiliary and did not strand a directly needed implementation or concrete verifier finding under the retention gate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel worked in the shared task workspace and committed each requirement artifact, with final clean status and no observed write collision or provenance instability.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same shared workspace sequentially, created all seven requirement patches, and committed the final Project 6 artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete concurrent-write collision, overwrite, or artifact leakage distinguishes the parallel attempt from serial; both delivered a coherent final tree that failed hidden checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel cleared TODO scans and syntax-only checks for touched Project 6 files, then explicitly reported that it did not run QEMU or full runtime tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran `make -C /workspace/Project6-File_System main`, checked for remaining TODOs, cleaned status, and also did not run board/emulator runtime tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger local build evidence for Project 6, but both lacked runtime acceptance coverage and both failed official evaluation; this gap is not tied to a retained parallel handoff or join error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used seven spawns, 1020 tool calls, and a longer run, but finished before timeout, made the final commit, and reported complete requirement coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer tool calls, finished earlier, and also reported complete requirement coverage before official failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more coordination budget, yet the observed closure state was still complete enough to commit; there is no direct evidence that fan-out displaced required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status evaluation marks both attempts as failed, so there is no discordant outcome to attribute to parallel coordination. Parallel used subagents and spent substantially more coordination budget, while serial was a single-threaded implementation path with a stronger Project 6 build check. Both delivered all seven patch artifacts and both left ordinary implementation defects that the official evaluator caught in different subsystems.
parallel_contributors: Parallel delegated surveys and late review checks, but the parent retained implementation and final commit responsibility.
Parallel verification stopped at TODO sweeps and syntax-only checks plus a stated lack of QEMU or full runtime tests.
Official failures remained in process exit, VM selection/writeback, and selected Project 6 file-system checks.
serial_contributors: Serial worked sequentially with no child agents or delegation and produced all seven patch artifacts.
Serial ran a Project 6 build and TODO sweeps but still skipped board or emulator runtime tests.
Official failures remained in process-management spawn/max-priority/exit checks and an expanded Project 6 cd check.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel passed some scheduler and VM checks that serial failed, while serial passed some VM and file-system checks that parallel failed.
The failures are concrete code-correctness gaps in the produced OS implementations rather than a visible lost handoff, unjoined implementation, collision, or budget-exhaustion episode.
evaluator_effects: Outcome is resolved from the current completed cell/status.json evaluation records; review metric fields are null because the provided outcome resolver does not extract final_test_results counts from these status files.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both official runs failed and no retained parallel-side coordination pattern cleared the realized-consequence gate
